extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO enrollment & discipline stakeholders, and the public interested in USPTO disciplinary actions
extracted.subtask_description: An official USPTO notice documenting the transfer of a registered patent practitioner to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.28, including effective date, authority, and practice restrictions. Used to communicate enforcement/administrative status changes for a registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.28
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective October 8, 2014, the Deputy General Counsel for Enrollment and Discipline and Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline for the United States Patent and Trademark Office transferred Andrew R. Spriegel (Registration No. 52,243) to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry records the formal authority and regulatory basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.28) for placing a registered practitioner on disability inactive status, the effective date of the transfer, the respondent's name and registration number, and the official (Deputy General Counsel for Enrollment and Discipline and Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline) effecting the transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practice while on disability inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: While on disability inactive status, the registrant may not practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explicitly states the scope of the suspension of practice rights: no practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, or other non-patent matters for the registrant for the duration of the disability inactive status. The prohibition is the practical effect of the transfer under 37 C.F.R. § 11.28.
